value.markup:
Every command, generated from the CLI itself. Each takes --help for this page's entry, and -o json for a result a script can read. crombolo schema prints the same description for a machine, as a clispec document.

admin

crombolo admin reset-password

Reset the administrator's password and print it. Each run acts again.

crombolo admin reset-password [--stdin]
ArgumentWhat it is
--stdinRead the new password from stdin.

api-client

crombolo api-client rotate

Issue a new secret for the API client, and print it once. Each run acts again.

crombolo api-client rotate [--client <client>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--clientThe client id; CROMBOLO_API_CLIENT_ID when not given.

assets

crombolo assets list

The stylesheets and scripts this site has. Changes nothing.

crombolo assets list

crombolo assets new

Write an empty stylesheet or script in the place the backoffice edits. Each run acts again.

crombolo assets new <kind> <name>
ArgumentWhat it is
kindWhich kind. One of stylesheet, script. Required.
nameIts file name. Required.

bundle

crombolo bundle check

Read-only: what installing a bundle's content here would do. Changes nothing.

crombolo bundle check <bundle> [--under <under>] [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--allow-missing-blobs] [--publish] [--no-schema] [--no-files] [--replace-files] [--save]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package directory, or the name of a bundle this site depends on. Required.
--underPlace the bundle under this page.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=take-bundle|keep-local|skip, or <key>/<property>[@<culture>]=take-bundle|keep-local.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of take-bundle, keep-local, skip.
--allow-missing-blobsImport media items whose files the bundle does not carry.
--publishPublish what it imports.
--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.
--replace-filesAllow replacing files this site has; the originals are kept for a revert.
--saveWrite the answers into the bundle.

crombolo bundle install

Re-check, back up, then apply a bundle's content. Each run acts again.

crombolo bundle install <bundle> [--under <under>] [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--allow-missing-blobs] [--publish] [--no-schema] [--no-files] [--replace-files] [--label <label>] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package directory, or the name of a bundle this site depends on. Required.
--underPlace the bundle under this page.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=take-bundle|keep-local|skip, or <key>/<property>[@<culture>]=take-bundle|keep-local.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of take-bundle, keep-local, skip.
--allow-missing-blobsImport media items whose files the bundle does not carry.
--publishPublish what it imports.
--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.
--replace-filesAllow replacing files this site has; the originals are kept for a revert.
--labelA label for the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo bundle purge

Back up, then drop a bundle's tables and clear its state. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo bundle purge <id> [--yes] [--dry-run] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
idThe bundle's id. Required.
--yesDon't ask: drop them.
--dry-runSay what it would do, and change nothing.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo content export

Write a subtree as a private bundle package, to move to another environment. Each run acts again.

crombolo content export [--root <root>] --out <out> [--only] [--drafts] [--with-blueprints] [--with-blobs] [--with-members] [--with-users] [--name <name>] [--package-version <package-version>] [--include-content] [--allow-content-unencrypted]
ArgumentWhat it is
--rootThe subtree to export; repeatable.
--outThe directory to write the package to. Required.
--onlyThe roots alone, not what is below them.
--draftsDrafts, not only what is published.
--with-blueprintsThe blueprints of its types.
--with-blobsWith --include-content: the media files.
--with-membersMembers, encrypted.
--with-usersBack-office users, encrypted.
--nameThe package's npm name.
--package-versionThe package's version.
--include-contentBring property values and media files, encrypted under a passphrase.
--allow-content-unencryptedWith --include-content: write them readable.

crombolo content import

Re-check, back up, then apply a bundle's content. Each run acts again.

crombolo content import <bundle> [--under <under>] [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--allow-missing-blobs] [--publish] [--no-schema] [--no-files] [--replace-files] [--label <label>] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package directory, or the name of a bundle this site depends on. Required.
--underPlace the bundle under this page.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=take-bundle|keep-local|skip, or <key>/<property>[@<culture>]=take-bundle|keep-local.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of take-bundle, keep-local, skip.
--allow-missing-blobsImport media items whose files the bundle does not carry.
--publishPublish what it imports.
--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.
--replace-filesAllow replacing files this site has; the originals are kept for a revert.
--labelA label for the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo content publish

Take a page live; --descendants for the branch below it. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo content publish <page> [--descendants] [--culture <culture>] [--at <at>] [--until <until>]
ArgumentWhat it is
pageThe page: a path or a uuid. Required.
--descendantsThe branch below it too.
--cultureOnly this culture; repeatable.
--atSchedule it for this time instead.
--untilSchedule the opposite for this time.

crombolo content revert

Put an import back, restoring what the site served. Each run acts again.

crombolo content revert <run> [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--force] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
runThe run id: `crombolo content runs` lists them. Required.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=discard|skip.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of discard, skip.
--forceRevert over changes made since the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo content runs

The imports applied here, newest first. Changes nothing.

crombolo content runs [--limit <limit>] [--offset <offset>] [--fields <fields>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--limitHow many to list. Default 20.
--offsetHow many to skip first. Default 0.
--fieldsOnly these fields of each item, comma-separated.

crombolo content unpublish

--cultureOnly this culture; repeatable.
--atSchedule it for this time instead.

Write the whole site to one file, to move it to another machine or host. Each run acts again.

crombolo export --site [--out <out>] [--no-media] [--drafts] [--with-members] [--with-users] [--anonymise] [--name <name>] [--package-version <package-version>]

--siteThe whole site (required: a part of it is `content export`). Required.
--outThe file to write.
--no-mediaLeave the media files out.
--draftsDrafts too.
--with-membersMembers, encrypted.

import

crombolo import

Replace this site with a whole-site file; says what first. Each run acts again.

crombolo import <file> [--replace] [--replace-all] [--yes] [--allow-missing-media] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
fileA whole-site file (crombolo export --site). Required.
--replaceReplace this site: what it loses is recycled, people kept.
--replace-allMake it exactly the file: what it loses is deleted, people too.
--yesWith --replace-all: don't ask.
--allow-missing-mediaImport media items whose files the file does not carry.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo import umbraco apply

Write a crombolo site from an Umbraco backup. Each run acts again.

crombolo import umbraco apply <backup> [--site <site>] [--media <media>] [--name <name>] [--drafts] [--staging <staging>] [--with-members] [--with-users] [--include-content] [--allow-content-unencrypted] --out <out> [--postgres] [--force]
ArgumentWhat it is
backupA .bacpac, or Umbraco's SQLite file. Required.
--siteThe Umbraco site's files, for its views, media and plugins.
--mediaWhere its media files are, if not under --site.
--nameThe new site's name.
--draftsBring drafts too.
--stagingWhere to unpack a .bacpac.
--with-membersBring members, encrypted.
--with-usersBring back-office users, encrypted.
--include-contentBring property values and media files, encrypted under a passphrase.
--allow-content-unencryptedWith --include-content: write them readable.
--outThe site directory to write. Required.
--postgresConfigure Postgres.
--forceWrite into a directory that is not empty.

pull

crombolo pull

A copy of a remote environment: started here, or replacing this site. Each run acts again.

crombolo pull [<remote>] [--env <env>] [--full] [--yes] [--no-media] [--media-info-only] [--lazy-media] [--timeout <timeout>] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--envThe environment to pull.
--fullA full copy, people included: needs the permission for it.
--yesReplace this site without asking.
--no-mediaLeave the media files out.
--media-info-onlyFetch media files one at a time, only what changed.
--lazy-mediaFetch each media file the first time it is asked for.
--timeoutSeconds to wait for the remote before giving up. Default 1800.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

push

crombolo push

Replace a remote environment with this site. Each run acts again.

crombolo push [<remote>] [--env <env>] [--force] [--auto-approve] [--media-info-only] [--dry-run] [--timeout <timeout>] [--no-browser]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--envThe environment to replace.
--forceGo on to a protected environment.
--auto-approveWith --force: don't ask for its name.
--media-info-onlySend media files one at a time, only what the remote lacks.
--dry-runSay what it would replace, and send nothing.
--timeoutSeconds to wait for the remote before giving up. Default 1800.
--no-browserDon't open an approval page.

schema

crombolo schema

This CLI described for machines, as a clispec v0.3 document. Changes nothing.

crombolo schema

crombolo schema add-property

Append a property to a type, and apply it. Each run acts again.

crombolo schema add-property <type> <alias> --type <type> [--name <name>] [--description <description>] [--mandatory] [--tab <tab>] [--dry-run]
ArgumentWhat it is
typeThe type's alias. Required.
aliasThe property's alias. Required.
--typeThe data type. Required.
--nameThe property's name.
--descriptionThe property's description.
--mandatoryAn editor must fill it in.
--tabThe tab it goes in.
--dry-runSay what it would do, and change nothing.

crombolo schema check

Validate schema/ and report what a sync would do to this database. Changes nothing.

crombolo schema check [--static]
ArgumentWhat it is
--staticValidate the files only, no database.

crombolo schema export

Write the database's definitions as schema/ files. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo schema export

crombolo schema new

Write a type file, with keys, and the view it points at, then apply it. Each run acts again.

crombolo schema new <kind> <alias> [--name <name>] [--description <description>] [--icon <icon>] [--at-root] [--element] [--tab <tab>] [--no-view]
ArgumentWhat it is
kindWhat kind of type. One of content-type, media-type, member-type. Required.
aliasThe type's alias. Required.
--nameThe type's name.
--descriptionThe type's description.
--iconThe type's icon.
--at-rootAllow it at the root of the tree.
--elementAn element type, for blocks.
--tabThe tab its first property goes in.
--no-viewNo view: a type nothing renders.

crombolo schema purge

Delete properties retired more than N days ago, with their values. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo schema purge --older-than <older-than> [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
--older-thanHow long, in days, a property must have been retired. Required.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo schema rewrite

Rewrite every schema/ file canonically. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo schema rewrite

crombolo schema sync

Apply schema/ to the database. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo schema sync [--force-retire-types]
ArgumentWhat it is
--force-retire-typesRetire a type the files no longer have even though content uses it.

--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.

users

crombolo users disable

Stop a user signing in, and end their sessions. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users disable <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users enable

Let a disabled user sign in again. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users enable <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users invite

Create a user and print the link they set their password with. Each run acts again.

crombolo users invite <email> [--group <group>] [--name <name>]
ArgumentWhat it is
emailTheir e-mail address. Required.
--groupA user group, by alias; repeatable.
--nameTheir name; the address when not given.

crombolo users list

The back-office users: who, their groups, their state and last sign-in. Changes nothing.

crombolo users list [--limit <limit>] [--offset <offset>] [--fields <fields>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--limitHow many to list. Default 50.
--offsetHow many to skip first. Default 0.
--fieldsOnly these fields of each item, comma-separated.

crombolo users reset-2fa

Remove a user's second factors, so their next sign-in sets one up again. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users reset-2fa <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users reset-password

Give a user a new password, and end their sessions. Each run acts again.

crombolo users reset-password <user> [--stdin]
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.
--stdinRead the new password from stdin.

crombolo users unlock

Clear a user's lockout and failed sign-ins. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users unlock <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

whoami

crombolo whoami

Who you are signed in as at a remote, and what you may do there. Changes nothing.

crombolo whoami [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

Exit codes

A failure exits with its kind's code; with -o json, or whenever stderr is not a terminal, the last line of stderr is a JSON envelope naming the kind. A check that finds what it looks for exits with an outcome's code, and its findings are its output.

CodeKindWhen
1internalSomething unexpected went wrong.
2usageThe arguments are wrong: an unknown command or flag, or one missing.
3timeoutGave up waiting. A remote job carries on at the remote.
4authNot signed in, the sign-in has lapsed, or a passphrase is missing or wrong.
5not_foundNo such remote, environment, page, run, bundle, file or account.
6conflictSomeone else is changing it, or it exists with a different value.
7confirmation_requiredIt would have asked first, and there is no terminal to ask on.
8refusedThe site or the remote said no: findings outstanding, a permission, a protected environment.
9unavailableThe database or the remote could not be reached.
10ioA file could not be read or written.
20problems_foundThe check found problems: status, types check, components check.
21blockedSomething must be resolved by a person first: content check, upgrade check, import umbraco report.
130interruptedStopped by a signal.
